Times are for your city. On festivals candles have their own times — check your community\'s calendar.

The times follow the opinion of the Alter Rebbe (Baal HaTanya), as in Chabad calendars: an hour of the day is a twelfth of the daylight; the Shema is said by the end of the third hour, the morning prayer by the end of the fourth, Minchah until sunset. They are calculated from the city\'s coordinates, accurate to 1–2 minutes: do not wait for the last minute, and check your community\'s calendar.

Above the time — the combination of the letters of the Name for this halachic hour (Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Fear 10).
What is the combination of the Name?

The four-letter Name — Havayah (י-ה-ו-ה). Its letters can be arranged in twelve ways: there are four letters, but two of them are ה, so there are 12 combinations, not 24.

The Kabbalists teach that each combination reveals the G-dly light in its own way and has its own time. Rabbi Moshe Cordovero, in Pardes Rimonim (Gate 21, ch. 8), writes of twelve combinations for the twelve hours of the day and the twelve hours of the night; in the teachings of the Arizal each of the twelve months of the year also has its own combination.

His student Rabbi Eliyahu de Vidas, in Reshit Chokhmah (Gate of Fear, ch. 10), writes that one combination shines in each hour, and learns awe of Heaven from it: every hour of the day comes from G-d, and one can remember this all day long, not only in prayer.

On the dial the combination changes with the halachic hour. The order follows Pardes Rimonim (Gate 13, ch. 3): three combinations for each letter of the Name, in the order י-ה-ו-ה; the first hour of the day and the first hour of the night begin with the first one. Which combination belongs to which hour is not spelled out in these books: this order was chosen by the project and has not been checked by a rabbi.

The combination is not pronounced — it is a reminder before your eyes, not a prayer and not a replacement for learning. The Name is not read aloud; the letters are named one by one: “Yud-Kei-Vav-Kei”. To turn it off, untick “The Name of the hour”.

The circle is half a day — the 12 halachic hours of the day (sun) or of the night (moon). It starts and ends at the top.
Gold is the day, blue the night. Each dash is a quarter of a halachic hour; every fourth, longer one starts an hour.
Past dashes glow; the short red hand is «now».
Dots on the rim are the times of the day. Tap a dot to see what it is and how long until it.
At the bottom of the screen — Shabbat, the alarms and the list of all times.

The morning alarm rings at a set time or a few minutes before the latest time for the Shema. The Torah study alarm reminds you to learn and opens the passage of the day of Neviim and Ketuvim. On Shabbat, Yom Tov and Yom Kippur both keep quiet — from candle lighting until the day ends.
For the alarm to ring and show on the screen, notifications are needed. The app will ask for the other permissions when you turn an alarm on.
The clock outside the app too
Widgets: long-press the home screen → «Widgets» → «Pele Shaon». A large one — the clock, a small one — only the Jewish date.
A notification with a countdown to the next time — turn it on in «Times». It shows on the lock screen.
At night by the bed: «☰» → «Help» → «Bedside night screen». While charging — a screen saver: phone Settings → Display → Screen saver → «Pele Shaon».
Light — the screen slowly brightens, like dawn; «Light only» wakes you without sound.
MyChitas Torah project · the «Clock» of the Niflaot site
The app collects no data about you: no accounts, no ads, no analytics, no trackers.
It does not go online — it does not even have the internet permission. The site opens only when you tap a button, in your browser.
The city, alarms and settings stay on the phone. If Android backup is on, the system may save them to your Google account.
Location is not requested: the city comes from the time zone or your choice.
Tap the Jewish date at the top to open the calendar: the month, festivals, the Torah portion and the times of any day.
Put the clock on the home screen (large)
Your home screen cannot add widgets from an app. Long-press an empty spot on the home screen → «Widgets» → find «Pele Shaon» (if it is not there, restart the phone once after installing).
Put the app icon on the home screen
Your home screen cannot add the icon from the app. Open the list of all apps, hold «Pele Shaon» and drag it to the home screen.
Pele Shaon on the home screen
The phone does not always put the icon of a new app on the home screen by itself — especially when the app is installed not from Google Play. One tap — and the icon is there.
Widgets — the clock without opening the app
Two widgets: a large one — the day clock with the time and the next zman, and a small one — only the Jewish date (after sunset — already the next day). Tap — and it goes on the home screen.

Times follow Chabad custom: from 7 days after the molad to the middle of the month, not on the eve of Shabbat or Yom Tov; in Av — after Tisha B’Av, in Tishrei — after Yom Kippur. Ask your community rabbi.

Defaults: Jerusalem 40 min, Haifa 30 min, Tel Aviv 22 min, most other cities 18 min. Follow local practice and ask your rabbi.

The molad is given as it is announced in the synagogue — in Jerusalem time (a «part», chelek, is 1/18 of a minute).
By Chabad custom, on Shabbat Mevarchim the whole book of Tehillim is said before the morning prayer.
In Chabad practice some avoid Kiddush during the seventh planetary hour on Friday night (Alter Rebbe, Orach Chaim 271:3).
Jerusalem is right in front of you
Hold the phone flat, or upright in front of you — then the arrow follows the camera. The gold arrow points to Jerusalem.

We pray facing Jerusalem, the place of the Temple (Berachot 30a; Shulchan Aruch, Orach Chaim 94:1). The direction is the shortest path on the globe (a great circle); many communities simply face east or south-east — follow your community and ask your rabbi.
The icon or the widgets did not appear?
